---
title: "Expected errors in a strict ranking"
subtitle: "1.16 · after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), section II.B and slides 21–22"
description: "Posterior expected wrong-direction counts among the n(n − 1)/2 statements of a strict ranking."
---

A strict ranking of $n$ units asserts a direction for all $M = n(n - 1)/2$ pairs; summing each claim's posterior error probability $1 - \pi_{ij}$ gives the expected number of wrong claims.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **97 firms.** Ranking KRW's firms by posterior mean makes 4,656 claims: 1,249 expected wrong vs. 1,395 by estimate (in **Data**, 639 pairs differ), with 35 claims above one half.
- **Top 10 by posterior mean.** 45 claims, 18.2 expected wrong; in **Data**, 5,834 California schools make 17,014,861 claims.
- **Six sites.** 15 claims, .719 expected wrong; C above D is least certain (.362).
- **League of 30.** 435 claims, 94.5 expected wrong vs. 102 by estimate (in **Data**: 37 differ; 88 wrong in this draw, 80.69 on average).

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Data: Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), doi:10.1257/aer.20230700; deposit doi:10.3886/E198284V1, CC-BY-NC, noncommercial use only (`pr_case_krw`, no endorsement; **describes KRW's experiment, not current conduct**). School count: California Department of Education, 2026 California School Dashboard chronic absenteeism data, academic year 2025–26 (`pr_case_cde`, [source conditions](https://www.cde.ca.gov/re/di/cr/index.asp)); no CDE endorsement is implied.
:::

```{=html}
<details>
<summary>Further notes</summary>
<p>KRW's race card at &lambda; = 1 is also a full ranking, in a slightly different order, so it expects 1,248 wrong claims where the posterior-mean order expects 1,249 (<a href="../cases/krw-lambda.qmd">KRW's archived reward path</a>). The expected count is a sum of probabilities over all stated claims, not a list of particular wrong claims.</p>
</details>
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
m <- pr_case_krw$input$summaries$means[, "race_signed"]
postrank_evaluate(rank(-m), pr_case_krw$input, weights = c(race_signed = 1, gender_signed = 0), tau = .2)$E["race_signed"]   # 1248.868
```
:::
